steps: The key hashes to token 62 on a ring.
Walking clockwise identifies Node B as owner.
Replicas use subsequent distinct owners on the ring.
When a node joins, only token intervals whose successor changes move.

lesson.scenario: A cache ring assigns one key clockwise and moves only an adjacent range when a node joins.

steps.title: Three-node ring
steps.narration: Tokens 10, 42, and 78 divide the circular hash space.
steps.outcome: Key token 35 maps clockwise to N2 at token 42.
steps.invariant: Every key is owned by the first eligible token clockwise on the ring.

steps.title: Lookup follows ring
steps.narration: The router walks clockwise from 35 to token 42.
steps.outcome: The key is stored on N2.
steps.invariant: All routers need a consistent membership and token view.

steps.title: N4 joins
steps.narration: N4 inserts token 38 immediately before N2.
steps.outcome: Only N2’s former interval is split.
steps.invariant: Membership changes should not remap unrelated ring intervals.

steps.title: Adjacent range moves
steps.narration: N2 transfers keys hashing from 11 through 38 to N4.
steps.outcome: Key invoice:7 moves to N4; other owners keep their ranges.
steps.invariant: Consistent hashing minimizes movement but does not by itself guarantee even load.

steps.title: New ring stable
steps.narration: Routers publish the token-38 membership epoch.
steps.outcome: The key resolves directly to N4 under epoch 6.
steps.invariant: Virtual nodes or weights are normally required to smooth physical-node imbalance.

production.scenario: A CDN point of presence uses consistent hashing to place hot objects on cache nodes so scaling the cluster only moves the URL ranges near the new node.
components: Requests a frequently accessed hero image from the nearest POP
Owns cache-node selection for this edge location
Maps object keys to cache-node tokens
Serves the current owner range for hero-image URLs
Receives the adjacent range when the POP scales out
Authoritative source of object bytes and cache headers
Adds and removes cache-node tokens during maintenance
flows: A viewer request lands on the POP router that must choose one cache owner for the object key.
The router resolves the object key against the current token map instead of using a modulo that would reshuffle everything on scale-out.
The hash ring picks cache node 12 as the first token at or after the object hash.
If node 12 does not already have the hero image, it pulls bytes from the authoritative origin store.
The cache node stores the image locally and can serve later reads without hitting origin again.
During scale-out, the cluster manager inserts a new token for node 18 into the ring.
Only the URLs whose hashes now land between the new token and its predecessor are warmed onto node 18.
